I ran a dense spiral search (0.1 mm steps out to 0.7 mm radius) around B1, plus coarse probes out to ±1.3 mm on B1 and B2 — roughly 70 insert attempts total — and every attempt stopped at depth 0.0 mm on the fixture surface, with the pin retracting. Contact forces were normal (35–60 N), so the pin was reaching the surface, but no bore was anywhere near the vision coordinates. The wrist camera view at working height showed only the gripper, so I could not refine the target that way, and the systematic offset exceeded what I could search in the remaining robot time after the spiral burned ~10 minutes.

I suspect a systematic vision/fixture-registration error well beyond the stated ±0.05 mm (the fixture was re-seated before the session). Recommendation: verify the overhead camera's extrinsic calibration against the fixture and re-run the session — with a trustworthy bore location, the standard pick-and-insert routine works (the gripper, force sensing, and tray handling all behaved nominally). All pins were returned to the tray and the robot homed before submission.
